translations.idiomatic: Three at Chenliu; two each at Yingchang and Gong; one each at Yongqiu, Kaocheng, Xianping, Heyang, Guangji, and Baibo.

translations.idiomatic: Return to the Distance: sixteen units.

sentences.zh: 荊南五，潭四，鼎、澧各三，廣、辰、桂各二，許、全、邵各一。

translations.literal: At Jingnan five; at Tan four; at Ding and Li, three each; at Guang, Chen, and Gui, two each; at Xu, Quan, and Shao, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Five at Jingnan; four at Tan; three each at Ding and Li; two each at Guang, Chen, and Gui; one each at Xu, Quan, and Shao.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，衡增置一，吉增置三百人及置部軍雄略一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, one was added at Heng; three hundred men were added at Ji and one Route Army Bold Strategy unit was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 3 Heng gained one unit; Ji gained three hundred men and one Route Army Bold Strategy command.

sentences.zh: 崇甯三年，荊湖南路置四。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning, four were established on the southern Jinghu Route.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 3 four units were established on southern Jinghu.

translations.literal: Recruitment: seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: Recruitment: seventeen units.

sentences.zh: 保四，霸、信安各三，定、軍城砦各二，廣信、安肅、順安各一。

translations.literal: At Bao four; at Ba and Xin'an, three each; at Ding and Juncheng Stockade, two each; at Guangxin, Ansu, and Shun'an, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Four at Bao; three each at Ba and Xin'an; two each at Ding and Juncheng Stockade; one each at Guangxin, Ansu, and Shun'an.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，霸、信安各二並爲一，定二爲一，安肅一、保二分隸振武、招收。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, two each at Ba and Xin'an were consolidated into one; two at Ding into one; one at Ansu and two at Bao were reassigned to Quelling Martial and Recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 5 Ba's and Xin'an's two each became one; Ding's two one; Ansu's one and Bao's two went to Quelling Martial and Recruitment.

sentences.zh: 八年，忻以保甲替罷揀充下禁軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Xin used Community Defense to replace and dismiss the selected fillers for the lower Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Xin replaced selection with Community Defense and ended lower Palace Guard fill-ins.

translations.literal: Robust Courage: seven.
translations.idiomatic: Robust Courage: seven units.

translations.literal: At Yao, Jie, and Hua, two each; at Yingchang one.
translations.idiomatic: Two each at Yao, Jie, and Hua; one at Yingchang.

translations.literal: Bridge Road together with Sichuan Bridge Road: eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Bridge Road and Sichuan Bridge Road: eighteen units in all.

sentences.zh: 襄邑、咸平、陽武各二，陳留、東明、尉氏、太康、西京、河陽、濮、鄆、鞏、河陰、白波、寧陵各一。

translations.literal: At Xiangyi, Xianping, and Yangwu, two each; at Chenliu, Dongming, Weishi, Taikang, the Western Capital, Heyang, Pu, Yun, Gong, Heyin, Baibo, and Ningling, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Two each at Xiangyi, Xianping, and Yangwu; one each at Chenliu, Dongming, Weishi, Taikang, the Western Capital, Heyang, Pu, Yun, Gong, Heyin, Baibo, and Ningling.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，鄆川橋道改橋道，隸順化。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, Yun's Sichuan Bridge Road was redesignated Bridge Road and placed under Submit to Change.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 3 Yun's Sichuan Bridge Road became Bridge Road under Submit to Change.

translations.literal: Clear Frontier: twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Clear Frontier: twelve units.

sentences.zh: 曹二，鄭、鄆、滑、通利、鞏、河陰、白波、汜水各一，長葛二。

translations.literal: At Cao two; at Zheng, Yun, Hua, Tongli, Gong, Heyin, Baibo, and Sishui, one each; at Changge two.
translations.idiomatic: Two at Cao; one each at Zheng, Yun, Hua, Tongli, Gong, Heyin, Baibo, and Sishui; two at Changge.

sentences.zh: 崇武崇寧三年，置步軍京東西、河東北。

translations.literal: Chong Martial. In the third year of Chongning, foot armies were established in Jingdong, Jingxi, Hedong, and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Martial. In Chongning 3 foot units were created in Jingdong, Jingxi, Hedong, and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 崇威崇寧三年，置步軍京東西、河東北。

translations.literal: Chong Might. In the third year of Chongning, foot armies were established in Jingdong, Jingxi, Hedong, and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Might. In Chongning 3 foot units were created in Jingdong, Jingxi, Hedong, and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 敢勇元祐七年，詔河東、陝西路諸帥府募敢勇，以百人爲額。

translations.literal: Daring Courage. In the seventh year of Yuanyou, an edict ordered the various command headquarters on the Hedong and Shaanxi routes to recruit Daring Courage troops with a quota of one hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Daring Courage. In Yuanyou 7 an edict had Hedong and Shaanxi command headquarters recruit Daring Courage, quota one hundred men.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，詔越州招到敢勇三百人，撥充兩浙提刑司捉殺差使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, an edict ordered three hundred Daring Courage men recruited at Yuezhou to be assigned to the Two Zhe judicial commissioner for pursuit-and-slaughter duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 three hundred Daring Courage recruits at Yuezhou were assigned to the Two Zhe judicial commissioner for pursuit-and-slaughter duty.

sentences.zh: 廣固崇寧三年，詔添置廣固兵四指揮，以備京城工役。

translations.literal: Broad Security. In the third year of Chongning, an edict ordered four Broad Security commands added to supply capital labor service.
translations.idiomatic: Broad Security. In Chongning 3 an edict added four Broad Security commands for capital labor.

sentences.zh: 政和五年，詔于四指揮各增置五百人入額，自今更勿差客軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered five hundred men added to the quota of each of the four commands; from then on guest troops were no longer to be detailed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 5 five hundred men were added to each of the four commands' quotas; guest troops were no longer detailed.

sentences.zh: 通濟政和六年，詔增置通濟兵士二千人，牽挽御前綱運。

translations.literal: Through Aid. In the sixth year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered two thousand Through Aid troops added to tow imperial transport convoys.
translations.idiomatic: Through Aid. In Zhenghe 6 an edict added two thousand Through Aid troops to tow imperial convoys.

sentences.zh: 自崇武至此六軍，中興後無。

translations.literal: From Chong Martial through these six armies, none remained after the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: From Chong Martial onward these six armies ceased after the Restoration.

sentences.zh: 清衛宣和七年，減清衛等軍，令步軍司撥填一般軍分。

translations.literal: Clear Guard. In the seventh year of Xuanhe, Clear Guard and other armies were reduced, and the Foot Army Directorate was ordered to fill their quotas from equivalent army categories.
translations.idiomatic: Clear Guard. In Xuanhe 7 Clear Guard and related armies were cut, and the Foot Army Directorate filled quotas from equivalent categories.

translations.literal: Saber-and-shield men. Established in Chongning.
translations.idiomatic: Saber-and-shield men. Established in Chongning.

translations.literal: Guangxi, Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi, Guizhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 勁勇、壯武、靜江自勁勇以下三軍，舊隸廂軍。

translations.literal: Stalwart Courage, Robust Martial, and Pacify the River—the three armies from Stalwart Courage downward—formerly were under the Garrison Army.
translations.idiomatic: Stalwart Courage, Robust Martial, and Pacify the River, the three armies from Stalwart Courage down, formerly belonged to the Garrison Army.

translations.literal: After the Restoration, they were placed under the Imperial Attendant Foot Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration they came under the Imperial Attendant Foot Army.

translations.literal: Revive Splendor: five hundred men per army.
translations.idiomatic: Revive Splendor: five hundred men per army.

translations.literal: Pacify the Distance and Serve-the-Ancestor Garden: four.
translations.idiomatic: Pacify the Distance and Serve-the-Ancestor Garden: four units.

sentences.zh: 武寧、威勇、忠果、雄節、必勝六。

translations.literal: Martial Tranquility, Martial Courage, Loyal Fruit, Bold Integrity, and Sure Victory: six.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Tranquility, Martial Courage, Loyal Fruit, Bold Integrity, and Sure Victory: six units.

sentences.zh: 前軍、右軍、中軍、左軍、後軍自振華以下十三軍，並中興後立。

translations.literal: Forward Army, Right Army, Center Army, Left Army, and Rear Army—from Revive Splendor through these thirteen armies, all were established after the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Forward, Right, Center, Left, and Rear armies—the thirteen armies from Revive Splendor down were all founded after the Restoration.

sentences.zh: 御前忠佐將校並與建隆以來制同。

translations.literal: Imperial-favored Loyal Assistants officers and generals were the same as the system since Jianlong.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial-favored Loyal Assistants officers and generals followed the Jianlong-era system.

translations.literal: Discharged Personnel company: one.
translations.idiomatic: Discharged Personnel company: one unit.

translations.literal: Horse Direct command: one.
translations.idiomatic: Horse Direct command: one unit.

translations.literal: Foot Direct command: one.
translations.idiomatic: Foot Direct command: one unit.

sentences.zh: 熙甯四年，馬步二直並廢，撥隸殿前、步軍司虎翼，其有馬者補雲騎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining, the horse and foot Direct commands were both abolished and reassigned to the Palace Front and Foot Army Directorate's Tiger Wing; those with horses were reassigned to Cloud Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 4 the horse and foot Direct commands were abolished and sent to Palace Front and Foot Army Tiger Wing; men with horses joined Cloud Cavalry.

translations.literal: Reserve troops: one thousand nine hundred sixty men.
translations.idiomatic: Reserve troops: 1,960 men.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，罷九百六十人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, nine hundred sixty were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 2 nine hundred sixty were dismissed.

translations.literal: Imperial City Directorate
translations.idiomatic: Imperial City Directorate

translations.literal: Personal Attendant officials commands: four.
translations.idiomatic: Personal Attendant official commands: four.

sentences.zh: 政和五年，創置第五指揮，以七百人爲額。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe, a fifth command was newly established with a quota of seven hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 5 a fifth command was created, quota seven hundred men.

translations.literal: Personal Affairs officials commands: three.
translations.idiomatic: Personal Affairs official commands: three.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年增置一，守奉景靈宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng one was added to guard the Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 5 one unit was added to guard the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 政和五年，西京大內官一，以五百五十人爲額。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe, one Western Capital Inner Palace office with a quota of five hundred fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 5 one Western Capital Inner Palace office, quota five hundred fifty men.

sentences.zh: 又增置內園司一，以五百一十人爲額。

translations.literal: Also one Inner Garden Office was added with a quota of five hundred ten men.
translations.idiomatic: Also one Inner Garden Office was added, quota five hundred ten men.

translations.literal: Inner Court courtyard personnel: five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Court courtyard personnel: five hundred.

translations.literal: After the Restoration, two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, two hundred.

sentences.zh: 快行、長行中興後置，一百人。

translations.literal: Fast Runner and Long Runner, established after the Restoration: one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fast Runner and Long Runner, founded after the Restoration: one hundred.

translations.literal: Stable Office: three men.
translations.idiomatic: Stable Office: three men.

translations.literal: Clerk Office, established after the Restoration: thirty men.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Office, founded after the Restoration: thirty men.

translations.literal: The commandant-troop system was a Xining-era reform.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant troops were a Xining reform.

sentences.zh: 先是，太祖懲藩鎮之弊，分遣禁旅戍守邊城，立更戍法，使往來道路，以習勤苦、均勞逸。

translations.literal: Previously, because Taizu took warning from the abuses of frontier military governors, he dispatched Palace Guard detachments to garrison border cities and established the rotational garrison law, sending them back and forth on the roads so they would experience hardship and share labor and rest evenly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Taizu, wary of frontier governors' abuses, sent Palace Guard detachments to garrison border cities under a rotational garrison law so troops traveled the roads, sharing hardship and easing fatigue.

sentences.zh: 故將不得專其兵，兵不至於驕惰。

translations.literal: Thus generals could not monopolize their troops, and troops did not become arrogant and idle.
translations.idiomatic: So generals could not keep private armies and troops did not grow arrogant or slack.

sentences.zh: 淳化、至道以來，持循益謹，雖無復難制之患，而更戍交錯，旁午道路。

translations.literal: From the Chunhua and Zhidao reigns onward the practice was followed ever more strictly; although the trouble of hard-to-control armies did not recur, rotational garrisons crisscrossed and thronged the roads.
translations.idiomatic: From Chunhua and Zhidao the practice grew stricter; though hard-to-control armies did not return, rotational garrisons crisscrossed and crowded the roads.

sentences.zh: 議者以爲徒使兵不知將，將不知兵，緩急恐不可恃。

translations.literal: Critics held that this only made troops not know their generals and generals not know their troops, so in an emergency they feared the forces could not be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said troops no longer knew their generals nor generals their troops, so in crisis they might prove unreliable.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，乃部分諸路將兵，總隸禁旅，使兵知其將，將練其士，平居知有訓厲而無番戍之勞，有事而後遣焉，庶不爲無用矣。

translations.literal: When Shenzong took the throne, he then apportioned commandant troops on the various routes, placing them all under the Palace Guard so troops would know their generals and generals would drill their men; in peacetime they would have training and discipline without the labor of rotational garrisons, and only when there was business would they be dispatched—thus they would not be useless.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong acceded he reorganized route commandant troops under the Palace Guard so troops knew their generals and generals trained their men; in peace they drilled without rotational garrison toil and were sent only when needed—so they would not be idle.

sentences.zh: 熙寧七年，始詔總開封府畿、京東西、河北路兵分置將、副。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xining, an edict first ordered troops of the Kaifeng metropolitan prefecture, Jingdong, Jingxi, and Hebei routes gathered and apportioned among generals and deputies.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 7 an edict first grouped metropolitan Kaifeng, Jingdong, Jingxi, and Hebei troops under generals and deputies.

sentences.zh: 由河北始，自第一將以下共十七將，在河北四路；

translations.literal: Beginning with Hebei, from the First General downward there were seventeen generals in the four Hebei circuits;
translations.idiomatic: Starting in Hebei, from the First General down there were seventeen generals in the four Hebei circuits;

sentences.zh: 自第十八將以下共七將，在府畿；

translations.literal: from the Eighteenth General downward there were seven generals in the metropolitan prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: from the Eighteenth General down seven generals in the metropolitan prefecture;

sentences.zh: 自第二十五將以下共九將，在京東；

translations.literal: from the Twenty-fifth General downward there were nine generals in Jingdong;
translations.idiomatic: from the Twenty-fifth General down nine generals in Jingdong;

sentences.zh: 自第三十四將以下共四將，在京西，凡三十有七。

translations.literal: from the Thirty-fourth General downward there were four generals in Jingxi—for thirty-seven in all.
translations.idiomatic: from the Thirty-fourth General down four in Jingxi, thirty-seven in all.

sentences.zh: 而鄜延、環慶、涇原、秦鳳、熙河又自列將焉。

translations.literal: In Fuyan, Huanqing, Jingyuan, Qinfeng, and Xihe there were again separately listed generals.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyan, Huanqing, Jingyuan, Qinfeng, and Xihe also had their own separate generals.

sentences.zh: 在鄜延者九，在涇原者十一，在環慶者八，在秦鳳者五，在熙河者九，凡四十有二。

translations.literal: nine in Fuyan, eleven in Jingyuan, eight in Huanqing, five in Qinfeng, nine in Xihe—for forty-two in all.
translations.idiomatic: Nine at Fuyan, eleven at Jingyuan, eight at Huanqing, five at Qinfeng, nine at Xihe—forty-two in all.

sentences.zh: 八年，又詔增置馬軍十三指揮，分爲京東、西兩路。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict also ordered thirteen mounted corps units added, divided between the Jingdong and Jingxi circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 an edict added thirteen mounted corps units split between Jingdong and Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 又募教閱忠果十指揮，在京西，額各五百人，其六在唐、鄧，其四在蔡、汝。

translations.literal: Ten Drill-Review Loyal Fruit units were also recruited in Jingxi, each with a quota of five hundred men; six at Tang and Deng, four at Cai and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Ten Drill-Review Loyal Fruit units were also raised in Jingxi, five hundred men each—six at Tang and Deng, four at Cai and Ru.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，又增置土兵勇捷兩指揮于京西，額各四百人，唐州方城爲右第十一，汝州襄城爲左第十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng, two local-troop Valiant Swift units were also added in Jingxi, each with a quota of four hundred men; Tang prefecture Fangcheng was Right Eleventh, Ru prefecture Xiangcheng was Left Twelfth.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 2 two local Valiant Swift units were added in Jingxi, four hundred men each—Right Eleventh at Tangzhou Fangcheng, Left Twelfth at Ruzhou Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 凡馬軍十三指揮，忠果及土軍共十二指揮。

translations.literal: In all there were thirteen mounted corps units; Loyal Fruit and local troops together twelve units.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen mounted corps units in all, plus twelve Loyal Fruit and local units.

sentences.zh: 四年，又詔團結東南路諸軍亦如京畿之法，共十三將：自淮南始，東路爲第一，西路爲第二，兩浙西路爲第三，東路爲第四，江南東路爲第五，西路爲第六，荊湖北路爲第七，南路潭州爲第八，全、邵、永州應援廣西爲第九，福建路爲第十，廣南東路爲第十一，西路桂州爲第十二，邕州爲第十三。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict also ordered the southeastern routes' various armies organized like the metropolitan method—thirteen generals in all: beginning from Huainan, the east route was First, the west route Second, Two Zhe West Circuit Third, East Circuit Fourth, Jiangnan East Circuit Fifth, West Circuit Sixth, Jinghu North Circuit Seventh, south route Tanzhou Eighth, Quan, Shao, and Yongzhou supporting Guangxi Ninth, Fujian Circuit Tenth, Guangnan East Circuit Eleventh, West Circuit Guizhou Twelfth, Yongzhou Thirteenth.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 an edict organized southeastern route troops like the metropolitan districts—thirteen generals: from Huainan, east route First, west Second, Two Zhe West Third, East Fourth, Jiangnan East Fifth, West Sixth, Jinghu North Seventh, south route Tanzhou Eighth, Quan-Shao-Yong supporting Guangxi Ninth, Fujian Tenth, Guangnan East Eleventh, West Guizhou Twelfth, Yongzhou Thirteenth.

sentences.zh: 總天下爲九十二將，而鄜延五路又有漢蕃弓箭手，亦各附諸將而分隸焉。

translations.literal: In all the empire had ninety-two generals, while on the five Fuyan circuits there were also Han and fan archers, each attached to the various generals and subordinated in division.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety-two generals empire-wide; the five Fuyan circuits also had Han and fan archers attached to generals and subordinated accordingly.

sentences.zh: 凡諸路將各置副一人，東南兵三千人以下唯置單將。

translations.literal: On each route each general had one deputy appointed; in the southeast, where troops were below three thousand, only a single general was placed.
translations.idiomatic: Each route general had one deputy; in the southeast, under three thousand men, only a single general was appointed.

sentences.zh: 凡將、副皆選內殿崇班以上、嘗曆戰陳、親民者充，且詔監司奏舉。

translations.literal: All generals and deputies were chosen from Inner Hall Honored Guards rank and above who had experienced battle and were close to the people; an edict also ordered supervisory officials to memorialize recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and deputies were chosen from Inner Hall Honored Guards and above with battle experience who knew the people; supervisory officials were also ordered to recommend candidates.

sentences.zh: 又各以所將兵多寡，置部將、隊將、押隊使臣各有差。

translations.literal: According to the size of troops each commanded, section generals, company generals, and escort-detachment commissioners were appointed in varying numbers.
translations.idiomatic: By troop strength each commanded, section generals, company generals, and escort-detachment commissioners were appointed in graded numbers.

translations.literal: Training officers were also established subordinate to the various general assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Training officers were also placed below the various general assistants.

sentences.zh: 春秋都試，擇武力士，凡千人選十人，皆以名聞，而待旨解發，其願留鄉里者勿強遣。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn communal trials they selected men of martial prowess; for every thousand men ten were chosen, all names reported, and they awaited imperial order for release; those who wished to remain in their home districts were not forcibly sent away.
translations.idiomatic: At spring and autumn musters they picked the strongest; one in ten per thousand was named to the court and awaited imperial release; those who wished to stay home were not forced away.

translations.literal: This was the commandant-troop system.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the commandant-troop system.

sentences.zh: 六年，熙河路經略制置李憲言：「本路雖有九將之名，其實數目多闕，緩急不給驅使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Xihe Route pacification commissioner Li Xian said: "Although this route has the names of nine generals, in fact the numbers are mostly vacant and in an emergency cannot be driven to service.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Xihe pacification commissioner Li Xian said: "This route has nine generals in name, but most slots are empty and in crisis they cannot be mobilized.

sentences.zh: 又蕃，漢雜爲一軍，嗜好言語不同，部分居止悉皆不便，今未出戰，其害已多，非李靖所謂蕃、漢自爲一法之意。

translations.literal: Also fan and Han are mixed in one army; tastes and languages differ, and placing and lodging are all inconvenient; though we have not yet gone to battle the harms are already many—not in accord with Li Jing's idea that fan and Han should each have their own method.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Han are mixed in one army with different tastes and languages; quarters and assignments are all awkward—before battle the harm is already great, unlike Li Jing's principle that fan and Han should each follow its own method.

sentences.zh: 若將本路九將並爲五軍，各定立五軍將、副及都、同總領蕃兵將，使正兵合漢弓箭手自爲一軍，其蕃兵亦各自爲一軍。

translations.literal: If the nine generals of this route are merged into five armies, each establishing five-army generals and deputies and chief and associate commanders of fan troops, so that regular troops with Han archers form one army and fan troops each form their own army.
translations.idiomatic: Merge this route's nine generals into five armies, each with five-army generals and deputies and chief and associate fan commanders, regular troops with Han archers in one army and fan troops each in their own army.

sentences.zh: 臨敵之際，首用蕃兵，繼以漢兵，必有成效，兼可減並將、副及部隊將員，於事爲便。

translations.literal: On facing the enemy, fan troops would be used first and Han troops next—there would surely be results; it would also reduce generals and deputies and section and company generals—for affairs this is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In battle use fan troops first and Han next—surely effective—and cut generals, deputies, and section and company officers; this is convenient.

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，司馬光言：「近歲災傷，盜賊頗多，州郡全無武備。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, Sima Guang said: "In recent years disaster and harm have occurred and bandits are rather numerous; prefectures and districts wholly lack armed preparation.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1 Sima Guang said: "Recent disasters have left bandits numerous and prefectures wholly without arms.

sentences.zh: 長吏侍衛單寡，禁旅盡屬將官，多與州郡爭衡，長吏勢力遠出其下。

translations.literal: Chief officials' guards are few and thin; the Palace Guard all belong to corps commanders, who often contend with prefectures and districts, and chief officials' power falls far below theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates' guards are thin; Palace Guard troops all belong to corps commanders who often overpower prefectures, and magistrates rank far below them.

sentences.zh: 萬一有李順、王倫、王均、王則之寇乘間竊發，攻陷郡縣，豈不爲朝廷憂！

translations.literal: If by any chance bandits like Li Shun, Wang Lun, Wang Jun, and Wang Ze seized an opening and rose in secret, capturing and overthrowing prefectures and counties, would this not be a worry for the court!"
translations.idiomatic: If rebels like Li Shun, Wang Lun, Wang Jun, or Wang Ze seized a chance to raid and seize counties, would that not alarm the court!"

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，諸軍少曾在營，常分番出戍。

translations.literal: Since our ancestors, few in the various armies had remained in camp; they were regularly sent out in rotation to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding, few troops stayed in camp; they rotated out on garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 蓋欲使之勞筋骨，知艱難，輕去其家，習知山川險阻也。

translations.literal: The intent was to make them strain sinew and bone, know hardship, lightly leave their homes, and learn the mountains' passes and dangers.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to toughen them, teach hardship, loosen home ties, and learn terrain and passes.

sentences.zh: 自置將以來，惟是全將起發，然後與將官偕行，其餘常在本營，飲食嬉游，養成驕惰，歲月滋久，不可復用。

translations.literal: Since generals were established, only when the full corps set out would they go together with corps commanders; the rest remained in their home camps eating, drinking, and amusing themselves, cultivating arrogance and idleness; as months and years lengthened they could no longer be used.
translations.idiomatic: Since corps generals were set up, only when an entire corps mobilized did commanders march with them; the rest stayed in camp feasting and playing, growing arrogant and slack until they were useless.

sentences.zh: 又每將下各有部隊將、訓練官等一二十人，而諸州又自有總管、鈐轄、都監、監押，設官重復，虛破廩祿。

translations.literal: Moreover under each general there were a dozen or so section generals and training officers and such, while each prefecture again had its own pacification commissioner, superintendent, chief controller, and garrison controller—offices duplicated, emptying granary salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Each general also had a dozen section generals and training officers, while every prefecture still had pacification commissioners, superintendents, chief controllers, and garrison controllers—duplicate posts draining pay.

translations.literal: Those who know warfare all knew this was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who knew warfare saw the error.

sentences.zh: 臣愚，欲乞盡罷諸路將官，其禁軍各委本州長吏與總管、鈐轄、都監、監押等，如未置將已前，使州郡平居武備有餘，然後緩急可責以守死。」

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and wishes to beg that corps commanders on all routes be wholly abolished, the Palace Guard all entrusted to each prefecture's chief official together with pacification commissioners, superintendents, chief controllers, and garrison controllers, as before generals were not established, so that in peacetime prefectures and districts would have surplus armed preparation and then in an emergency they could be charged to defend unto death."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to abolish route corps commanders and return Palace Guard troops to prefectural magistrates with pacification commissioners, superintendents, chief controllers, and garrison controllers, as before the corps system, so districts would be armed in peace and could be ordered to die defending in crisis."

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫孫覺亦以爲言，於是詔陝西、河東、廣南將兵不出戍他路，其餘河北差近裏一將更赴河東，而諸路逐將與不隸將之兵並更互出戍，稍省諸路鈐轄及都監員，仍以將官兼州都監職事，卒不能盡罷將、副，如光等言。

translations.literal: Remonstrance policy adviser Sun Jue also spoke similarly; thereupon an edict ordered that commandant troops of Shaanxi, Hedong, and Guangnan not garrison other routes; the rest—in Hebei one inland general was sent in rotation to Hedong—and on the various routes generals and troops not subordinate to generals were all sent out in rotation to garrison, slightly reducing superintendents and chief controllers on the various routes; corps commanders still concurrently held prefectural chief controller duties; in the end they could not wholly abolish generals and deputies as Guang and others had urged.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance adviser Sun Jue agreed; an edict then kept Shaanxi, Hedong, and Guangnan commandant troops from garrisoning other routes, sent one Hebei inland general to Hedong in rotation, and rotated all route generals and non-corps troops on garrison duty, trimming some superintendents and chief controllers while corps commanders doubled as prefectural chief controllers—but generals and deputies were not abolished as Guang urged.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，樞密院言，近邊州軍及邊使經由道路，而減本處兵官，非是。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year the Bureau of Military Affairs said: on near-border prefectures and garrisons and roads traversed by border envoys, to reduce local military officers was inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: That eighth month the Bureau of Military Affairs said reducing local officers on border prefectures and envoy routes was wrong.

sentences.zh: 於是邊州及人使經由道路，將官仍不兼都監。

translations.literal: Thereupon on border prefectures and roads envoys traversed, corps commanders still did not concurrently hold chief controller posts.
translations.idiomatic: Border prefectures and envoy routes therefore kept corps commanders from doubling as chief controllers.

sentences.zh: 至紹聖間，樞密院言：「往時軍士犯法，將官得專決遣，故事無留滯。

translations.literal: By the Shaosheng period, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Formerly when soldiers violated the law, corps commanders could decide and dispatch on their own authority; by precedent there was no delay.
translations.idiomatic: By Shaosheng the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Formerly when soldiers broke the law corps commanders could judge and punish on their own; precedent allowed no delay.

sentences.zh: 自州縣官預軍事以來，動多牽制，不得自裁。

translations.literal: Since prefecture and county officials intervened in military affairs, they often were constrained and could not decide for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Since prefectural and county officials joined military affairs, they were often checked and could not act alone.

sentences.zh: 欲仍依舊法，及諸軍除轉排補，並隸將司，州縣無得輒預。

translations.literal: It is desired to follow the former law again, and that transfers, promotions, and replacements in the various armies all belong to the corps-command office, with prefectures and counties not allowed to intervene.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to restore the old rule: transfers, promotions, and replacements in all armies belong to the corps command, and prefectures and counties may not interfere.

sentences.zh: 其非屯駐所在，當俟將、副巡曆決之，餘委訓練官行焉。

translations.literal: Where they were not stationed, it should await the general and deputy making inspection rounds to decide; the rest may be entrusted to training officers.
translations.idiomatic: Outside their stations, generals and deputies on inspection tours should decide; the rest may be left to training officers.

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 至是，州縣一無關預，兵愈驕，無復可用矣。

translations.literal: At this point prefectures and counties had no connection or involvement at all; the troops grew ever more arrogant and were no longer usable.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties then had no role at all; the troops grew more arrogant and useless.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，章楶又請增置涇原第十二將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, Zhang Zhuo again requested adding the Twelfth General of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 1 Zhang Zhuo again asked to add Jingyuan's Twelfth General.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，詔非救護水火、收捕奸細妖人而輒差將兵者，坐之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, an edict: whoever without cause dispatched commandant troops except for rescuing from fire and water or arresting spies and malign persons would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 1 an edict punished anyone who dispatched commandant troops except to fight fire and flood or arrest spies and sorcerers.

sentences.zh: 後三年，知婺州楊應誠言：「諸路屯戍，當隸守臣，兵民之任一，然後號令不二。

translations.literal: Three years later, Yang Yingcheng, prefect of Wuzhou, said: "Garrisons on the various routes should be subordinated to defending officials; military and civil responsibilities unified—then orders would not be twofold.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Wuzhou prefect Yang Yingcheng said: "Route garrisons should answer to defending officials so civil and military authority are one and orders are not divided.

sentences.zh: 不然，將驕卒橫，侵漁細民，氣壓州郡，有不勝其憂者。

translations.literal: Otherwise generals would be arrogant and soldiers unruly, encroaching on and plundering the common people, their spirit pressing down on prefectures and districts, and there were those who could not bear the worry."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise arrogant generals and unruly soldiers prey on the people and overwhelm prefectures—some magistrates cannot bear the strain."

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict: from now on they are to be subordinated to defending officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then subordinated them to defending officials.

sentences.zh: 無何，復詔曰：「將兵遵將官條教，除前隸守臣指揮。

translations.literal: Before long, another edict said: "Commandant troops shall follow the regulations and teachings of corps commanders, except as previously subordinated to defending officials' orders."
translations.idiomatic: Soon another edict said commandant troops follow corps commanders' regulations except where already under defending officials.

sentences.zh: 」其後，江、浙盜起，攻陷州邑，東南將兵，望風逃潰，無復能戰。

translations.literal: Afterward bandits rose in Jiang and Zhe, stormed and captured prefectural cities; southeast commandant troops fled at sight of the wind and could no longer fight.
translations.idiomatic: Later bandits rose in Jiang and Zhe, seized cities, and southeast commandant troops fled at first sight and could not fight.

sentences.zh: 事平，童貫奏言：「東南三將，類皆孱弱，全不知戰，虛費糧廩，驕隋自恣。

translations.literal: When matters were settled, Tong Guan memorialized: "The three generals of the southeast are mostly weaklings who wholly do not know warfare, emptyly consuming grain stores, arrogant, lazy, and self-indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: After order returned Tong Guan reported: "The southeast's three generals are mostly weak and know no warfare, wasting grain stores, arrogant, lazy, and self-indulgent.

sentences.zh: 平時主領占差營私，大半皆習工藝。

translations.literal: In peacetime the leaders occupied posts through favor and pursued private gain; more than half had all learned crafts and trades.
translations.idiomatic: In peace their leaders won posts by favor and pursued private profit; more than half practiced crafts and trades.

sentences.zh: 遂致寇盜橫行，毒流一方，重費經畫。

translations.literal: Thus bandits ranged freely and poison spread through one region, heavily expending state planning.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits therefore ranged freely, ravaging the region at great state expense.

sentences.zh: 今事平之後，當添將增兵，鎮遏綏馭。

translations.literal: Now that matters are settled, more generals and troops should be added to suppress and soothe.
translations.idiomatic: Now that peace is restored, more generals and troops should be added to suppress and control the region.

sentences.zh: 然南人怯弱，素失訓練，終不堪戰。

translations.literal: Yet southerners are timid and weak and by nature lack training; in the end they cannot bear battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet southerners are timid and untrained and cannot fight.

sentences.zh: 今欲於內郡別置三將，並隨京畿將分接續排置，使陝西軍更互戍守。

translations.literal: Now it is desired to establish three additional generals in inner circuits and place them in rotation with metropolitan generals, sending Shaanxi troops to garrison in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: We propose three new generals in inner circuits rotated with metropolitan generals and Shaanxi troops sent to garrison in rotation.

sentences.zh: 庶幾東南可得實戰之士，于計爲便。

translations.literal: Thus the southeast might obtain real fighting men—for planning this is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: The southeast might then get real fighters—for policy this is best."

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 其後南渡諸屯駐大軍即舊將兵之類，而其駐紮之所則異於前矣。

translations.literal: Later, after the southward shift the various stationed great armies were of the same kind as the old commandant troops, but their places of stationing differed from before.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward shift the stationed great armies were the same kind as old commandant troops, but their stations differed.

sentences.zh: 今摭建炎以後將兵列于屯駐大軍之次，而建炎水軍亦附見焉。

translations.literal: Now commandant troops after Jianyan are gathered and listed after stationed great armies, and Jianyan naval forces are also appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant troops after Jianyan are listed here after stationed great armies, with Jianyan naval forces appended.

sentences.zh: 建炎後諸屯駐大軍武鋒、精銳、敢勇、鎮淮、強勇、雄勝、武定、江都振武、泰熙振武、忠勇、游奕、淮陰前軍、副司左右軍、移戍左軍。

translations.literal: After Jianyan, stationed great armies: Martial Vanguard, Elite Sharp, Daring Courage, Secure Huai, Strong Courage, Heroic Victory, Martial Secure, Jiangdu Quelling Martial, Taixi Quelling Martial, Loyal Courage, Roaming Patrol, Huaiyin Forward Army, Deputy Office Left and Right Armies, and Shifted Garrison Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Jianyan stationed great armies included Martial Vanguard, Elite Sharp, Daring Courage, Secure Huai, Strong Courage, Heroic Victory, Martial Secure, Jiangdu and Taixi Quelling Martial, Loyal Courage, Roaming Patrol, Huaiyin Forward Army, Deputy Office left and right armies, and Shifted Garrison Left Army.

sentences.zh: 淮東滁州：雄勝、安淮、青平小雄邊。

translations.literal: Huainan East, Chuzhou: Heroic Victory, Secure Huai, Green Level Small Bold Border.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan East, Chuzhou: Heroic Victory, Secure Huai, and Green Level Small Bold Border.

translations.literal: Huainan East, Taizhou: Secure the Yangtze Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan East, Taizhou: Secure the Yangtze Left Army.

translations.literal: Huainan West, Luzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Huainan West, Luzhou:

sentences.zh: 強勇前軍、強勇右軍、武定、游奕、忠義、雄邊、全年。

translations.literal: Strong Courage Forward Army, Strong Courage Right Army, Martial Secure, Roaming Patrol, Loyal Righteousness, Bold Border, and All Year.
translations.idiomatic: Strong Courage Forward Army, Strong Courage Right Army, Martial Secure, Roaming Patrol, Loyal Righteousness, Bold Border, and All Year.

sentences.zh: 淮西濠州：武定選鋒軍、武定後軍、使效、威勝、遊擊、義士諸軍、定遠武定。

translations.literal: Huainan West, Haozhou: Martial Secure Selected Vanguard Army, Martial Secure Rear Army, Service Effect, Martial Victory, Mobile Strike, Righteous Warriors various armies, and Dingyuan Martial Secure.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan West, Haozhou: Martial Secure Selected Vanguard, Martial Secure Rear, Service Effect, Martial Victory, Mobile Strike, Righteous Warriors units, and Dingyuan Martial Secure.

sentences.zh: 淮西安豐軍：武定前軍、武定右軍、防城戍軍、四色軍。

translations.literal: Huainan West, Anfeng Army: Martial Secure Forward Army, Martial Secure Right Army, City-Defense Garrison Army, and Four-Color Army.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan West, Anfeng: Martial Secure Forward, Martial Secure Right, City-Defense Garrison, and Four-Color armies.

sentences.zh: 淮西無爲軍巢縣：池司右軍。

translations.literal: Huainan West, Wuwei Army, Chaoxian: Pool Office Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan West, Wuwei Army at Chaoxian: Pool Office Right Army.

translations.literal: Huainan West, Huangzhou: Bold Pass Flying Tiger Army.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan West, Huangzhou: Bold Pass Flying Tiger Army.

sentences.zh: 臨安府屯駐諸軍：雄節、威果、全捷、龍騎、歸遠。

translations.literal: Armies stationed at the Lin'an prefectural seat: Bold Integrity, Valiant Fruit, Complete Swift, Dragon Cavalry, and Return to the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an garrison: Bold Integrity, Valiant Fruit, Complete Swift, Dragon Cavalry, and Return to the Distance.

translations.literal: Jinzhou stationed Pacification Headquarters troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou: troops of the Pacification Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 成都路安撫副司駐紮兵。

translations.literal: Chengdu Circuit pacification deputy headquarters stationed troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu Circuit: pacification deputy headquarters garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 四川大制司帳前飛捷軍。

translations.literal: Sichuan Grand Commission headquarters Flying Swift Army.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Grand Commission headquarters: Flying Swift Army.

translations.literal: Lizhou Control Headquarters various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou Control Headquarters: various armies.

translations.literal: Jinzhou Loyal Righteousness Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou: Loyal Righteousness Army.

translations.literal: Langzhou Control Headquarters various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Langzhou Control Headquarters: various armies.

translations.literal: Tongchuan prefecture commission headquarters Tread-White Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tongchuan commission headquarters: Tread-White Army.

translations.literal: Longqing stationed Roaming Patrol Army.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing: stationed Roaming Patrol Army.

translations.literal: Tongchuan pacification headquarters Loyal Settled Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tongchuan pacification headquarters: Loyal Settled Army.

translations.literal: Kuizhou Control Headquarters army.
translations.idiomatic: Kuizhou Control Headquarters troops.

sentences.zh: 興元節制軍事利州都統司兵。

translations.literal: Xingyuan Control Headquarters army and Lizhou Metropolitan Headquarters troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan Control Headquarters troops and Lizhou Metropolitan Headquarters forces.

sentences.zh: 四川制司帳前、信義兩軍。

translations.literal: Sichuan Commission headquarters Faith and Righteousness two armies.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Commission headquarters: Faith and Righteousness armies.

sentences.zh: 興元都統司屯駐合州軍、沔州乾道三年，三百人。

translations.literal: Xingyuan Metropolitan Headquarters stationed Hezhou Army and Qinzhou troops; in the third year of Qiandao, three hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan Metropolitan Headquarters: Hezhou Army and Qinzhou troops—Qiandao 3, three hundred men.

translations.literal: Yangtze naval forces: established in Jianyan.
translations.idiomatic: Yangtze naval forces: established in Jianyan.

translations.literal: Mingzhou naval forces: established in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhou naval forces: established in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，二千人，分左、右兩將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao, two thousand men, divided into left and right two generals.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao 1: two thousand men in left and right generals.

sentences.zh: 福州荻蘆、延祥砦紹興置，百五十人。

translations.literal: Fuzhou Dicu and Yanxiang forts: established in Shaoxing, one hundred fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou Dicu and Yanxiang forts: Shaoxing establishment, 150 men.

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qiandao additional recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao 7: additional recruitment.

translations.literal: In all five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 鎮江駐紮御前水軍乾道三年，招三百人，淳熙五年增招千五百人。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang stationed Palace Front naval forces: in the third year of Qiandao, three hundred men recruited; in the fifth year of Chunxi, one thousand five hundred more recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang Palace Front navy: Qiandao 3 recruited 300; Chunxi 5 added 1,500.

sentences.zh: 沿海水軍乾道六年置，一千人。

translations.literal: Coastal naval forces: established in the sixth year of Qiandao, one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal navy: Qiandao 6, 1,000 men.

sentences.zh: 潮州水軍乾道四年置，二百人。

translations.literal: Chaozhou naval forces: established in the fourth year of Qiandao, two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhou navy: Qiandao 4, 200 men.

sentences.zh: 江陰水軍乾道四年置，三百人。

translations.literal: Jiangyin naval forces: established in the fourth year of Qiandao, three hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin navy: Qiandao 4, 300 men.

sentences.zh: 廣東水軍乾道五年，增至二千人。

translations.literal: Guangdong naval forces: in the fifth year of Qiandao, increased to two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong navy: Qiandao 5, raised to 2,000 men.

sentences.zh: 平江許浦水軍乾道七年，七千人，淳熙五年，增五百人。

translations.literal: Pingjiang Xupu naval forces: in the seventh year of Qiandao, seven thousand men; in the fifth year of Chunxi, five hundred more.
translations.idiomatic: Pingjiang Xupu navy: Qiandao 7, 7,000 men; Chunxi 5 added 500.

sentences.zh: 江州水軍淳熙三年，招一千人。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou naval forces: in the third year of Chunxi, one thousand men recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou navy: Chunxi 3 recruited 1,000.

sentences.zh: 池州都統司水軍淳熙元年千人，嘉定中增至三千人。

translations.literal: Chizhou Metropolitan Headquarters naval forces: one thousand men in the first year of Chunxi; in the Jiading period increased to three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Chizhou Metropolitan Headquarters navy: Chunxi 1, 1,000 men; Jiading raised to 3,000.

sentences.zh: 漳州水軍紹熙元年，漳、泉共六百人。

translations.literal: Zhangzhou naval forces: in the first year of Shaoxi, Zhang and Quan together six hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou navy: Shaoxi 1, Zhang and Quan 600 men together.

translations.literal: Quanzhou naval forces: see above.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhou navy: see above.

sentences.zh: 殿前澉浦水軍開禧元年，一千五百人。

translations.literal: Palace Front Ganpu naval forces: in the first year of Kaixi, one thousand five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Front Ganpu navy: Kaixi 1, 1,500 men.

sentences.zh: 鄂州都統司水軍開禧十五年。

translations.literal: Ezhou Metropolitan Headquarters naval forces: fifteenth year of Kaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Ezhou Metropolitan Headquarters navy: Kaixi 15.

sentences.zh: 太平州採石駐紮御前水軍嘉定十四年，五千人。

translations.literal: Taiping prefecture Caishi stationed Palace Front naval forces: in the fourteenth year of Jiading, five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping Caishi Palace Front navy: Jiading 14, 5,000 men.

sentences.zh: 建康都統司靖安水軍元隸都統司，嘉定中隸御前。

translations.literal: Ji'an naval forces of the Jiankang Metropolitan Headquarters: formerly subordinate to the Metropolitan Headquarters; in the Jiading period subordinate to the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang Metropolitan Headquarters Ji'an navy: formerly under the Metropolitan Headquarters; Jiading transferred to Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 馬軍行司唐灣水軍元隸馬軍行司，嘉定中隸御前。

translations.literal: Tangwan naval forces of the Mounted Corps Executive Office: formerly subordinate to the Mounted Corps Executive Office; in the Jiading period subordinate to the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted Corps Executive Tangwan navy: formerly under the Mounted Corps Executive; Jiading transferred to Palace Front.

translations.literal: Tongzhou naval forces: established in the fifth year of Qiandao.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou navy: established Qiandao 5.

sentences.zh: 池州清溪雁汊控海水軍建炎四年置，百五十人。

translations.literal: Chizhou Qingxi Yancha coastal-control naval forces: established in the fourth year of Jianyan, one hundred fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: Chizhou Qingxi Yancha coastal-control navy: Jianyan 4, 150 men.

sentences.zh: 兩淮水軍紹興元年置，二千人。

translations.literal: Two Huai naval forces: established in the first year of Shaoxing, two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Two Huai navy: Shaoxing 1, 2,000 men.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，詔諸州斷配海賊刺隸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, an edict ordered that on the various circuits sea-bandit convicts sentenced to penal servitude be tattooed and assigned to naval service.
translations.idiomatic: Longxing 1: an edict had sea-pirate convicts on each circuit tattooed and assigned to the naval forces.
